name: Shale
author: E. T. Carter
description: Fractured stone plates fill the frame, each shaded as one flat slate facet under a slowly wandering raking light and grained with fine sedimentary bedding laminations that cross every slab like layered rock, while the fissures between them glow ember from below — easing apart and reseating with tectonic patience, brightest where the gaps run widest.

params.label: Plate size
params.effect: Average plate diameter in CSS pixels; small plates read as rubble, large plates as monumental slabs.

params.label: Drift
params.effect: How quickly plates ease apart and reseat — the breathing rate of the fissures, from near-geological to visibly restless.

params.label: Fissure width
params.effect: Maximum width of the glowing gaps between plates at full separation; narrow cracks of ember light or wide molten channels.
